p == att.Config selects the canonical config digest; path forms agree because both sides use git top-relative POSIX paths (checked against testdata/mutation-incremental/real/a-survivor attestation: config 'mutation-incremental.json', files keys and report files/testFiles keys all repo-relative).

Go configDigest (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline, views dropped, no HTML escaping) is pinned to Node snapshot.mjs:58 by testdata/mutation-incremental/config-digest-vectors.json; go test ./internal/mutationfresh and node --test configdigest.test.mjs attest.test.mjs both pass locally.

Fingerprint layout mutation:<kind>:<mode>:<engine>:... matches findings.freshnessEngine (SplitN 5, parts[3]) at findings.go:221 and the three freshnessPrefixes; supersede keyed on this run's Engines() from reviewers/mutation.go.

LoadMutationContext: task-done/epic-ready use Worktree(root), pr-ready uses Head(root) unless --include-working-tree; EffectiveMode forces advisory at task-done; main.go mustFreshnessMode exits 2 on an invalid env value before any review, matching spec 6.4.

pr-ready reviewInputDigest serializes MutationContext Mode/Freshness (omitempty, ReportFreshness.Path is json:"-"), so reuse is invalidated on mode/attestation/classification change and runs without reports keep their digest (spec 6.7). Learning skips all three prefixes; confidenceForFinding is only reached via knowledgeFromFindings, which already skips.

Harness default exclusions (config.mjs) cover stateDir, .stryker-tmp and the Stryker reports, and the example config ignores .metareview/** and docs/**; docs/mutation-harness.md now tells users to keep metareview's own files in ignore, so gate review logs committed after a harness run do not blanket-stale kills.

findings.note: Worktree-mode 'fresh path' set disagrees with the harness for a tracked file deleted from the working tree but still in the index (plain rm, not git rm). worktree.Paths() lists `git ls-files -c` entries without filtering absent ones (an Lstat error is not skipped), and changedPaths adds any unattested non-mutate/test path as changed with digest `absent`; the harness lists the same path but skips it (digestOf null), so it is never attested. Result: if the deleted file is support/global/unclassified (e.g. an old tests/helpers file or an un-ignored doc), task-done (and pr-ready --include-working-tree) report every kill stale with cause <path>=absent, and the recommended fix 're-run the harness' can never clear it until the deletion is staged or committed. Spec 6.3 says 'present paths not in files', so absent fresh paths should be skipped (e.g. `if !attested && digest == Absent { continue }`). Not blocking: task-done is always advisory, epic-ready already blocks dirty trees, and pr-ready defaults to HEAD mode where ls-tree lists only present paths; the only enforced path is the opt-in --include-working-tree + enforce combination.
